H6TX22283.name: Trever Nehls
H6TX22283.bio: Retired U.S. Army colonel with 33 years of service and former constable and police officer.

positions.stance: Supports passing President Trump's executive actions into permanent law, finishing the wall, ending catch-and-release, and deporting illegal aliens who violate U.S. laws.
Supports lower taxes, fewer regulations and "a pro-growth agenda" to lower costs for groceries, gas, housing and everyday necessities.
"Parents, not bureaucrats, must be in control"; will vote to eliminate DEI mandates, block gender ideology in schools, and require full curriculum transparency.
Supports unleashing Texas oil, gas and nuclear energy and cutting regulations that drive up gas prices to restore U.S. energy dominance.
Will "back the blue without apology" and fully fund and support law enforcement; opposes soft-on-crime policies.

H4TX23120.name: Brandon Herrera
H4TX23120.bio: Small business owner in firearm manufacturing and online creator promoting firearm safety and Second Amendment advocacy.

positions.stance: Will oppose any spending bill that does not fund comprehensive border security, and will fight to reinstate "Remain in Mexico" and end asylum abuse.
Has taken the "No New Taxes" pledge, will fight wasteful spending, and will sponsor the REINS Act requiring congressional approval of major regulations.
Will work to expand Tricare so every veteran can see the doctor of their choice and dedicate two full-time staffers to veterans.
Will fight for national concealed carry reciprocity and block Red Flag laws or new firearms restrictions.
"Brandon will fight to protect women's sports."

H6TX23273.name: Katy Padilla Stout
H6TX23273.bio: Former teacher and attorney for children in the foster care system.

positions.stance: Opposes tax cuts for billionaires and supports "a tax code which empowers the middle class and raises people from poverty into the middle class."
"I support expanding our Medicare system to cover all Americans"; short of that, supports strengthening the Affordable Care Act.
Supports universal background checks, a ban on bump stocks, red-flag laws, and more funding for mental health and crisis intervention.
Supports a historic investment in universal Pre-K, raising the minimum wage, and requiring paid parental leave.
Opposes the planned border wall in the Big Bend region and pledges to stand up to the Trump Administration on it.

H0TX24209.name: Beth Van Duyne
H0TX24209.bio: Former mayor of her hometown who later served in a presidential administration.

H6TX24172.name: Kevin Burge
H6TX24172.bio: U.S. Marine Corps veteran with two deployments to Iraq and one to Afghanistan.

positions.stance: Will fast-track affordable housing, crack down on corporate landlords, raise the federal minimum wage, and lower taxes for families earning under $400,000.
Will pass strong data center requirements prioritizing water recycling, air and noise pollution laws, and investment in alternative energy.
Will "fight to codify Roe v. Wade into Federal Law" and hold federal officers accountable for constitutional violations.
Will expand ACA tax credits and Medicaid, fund community health centers, and pursue universal health coverage without banning private insurance.
Will oppose vouchers, rebuild the Department of Education, provide fee-free community college, and give a $2,000 payment to every public school teacher.

H2TX33040.name: Roger Williams
H2TX33040.bio: U.S. Representative for Texas's 25th District since 2013, former Texas Secretary of State, and longtime owner of a family car dealership.

H6TX25237.name: Dione Sims
H6TX25237.bio: Founder of the Fort Worth nonprofit Unity Unlimited, Inc. and co-producer of the annual Juneteenth Fort Worth Celebration.

positions.stance: Will advocate for Texas to close its coverage gap through Medicaid expansion and support targeted help making Marketplace coverage more affordable.
Supports strengthening Medicare's ability to negotiate high-cost drug prices and increasing competition from generic and biosimilar medicines.
Supports expanding sliding-scale childcare assistance for working- and middle-class families and federal-state partnerships to expand childcare supply.
Believes Texans should have "a meaningful voice" in whether major data centers are built in their communities, with companies investing in host communities.
Will fight for aggressive oversight of corruption and stronger transparency and ethics rules, including meaningful financial disclosures for public officials.

H4TX26149.name: Brandon Gill
H4TX26149.bio: U.S. Representative for Texas's 26th District; former investment banker and hedge fund analyst.

positions.stance: Introduced legislation to codify the Remain in Mexico policy and wants an immigration system that "supports the American worker."
Says Congress must pass legislation addressing housing affordability, prioritize the American worker, cut wasteful spending, and support a balanced budget.
Supports a "Texas First" energy approach, cutting red tape across the industry, and energy independence: "drill, baby, drill!"
"Our Second Amendment shall not be infringed."
Firmly supports Israel's right to defend itself against Hamas and calls for the international community to denounce Hamas's terrorism.

H6TX26144.name: Steven Shook
H6TX26144.bio: Registered nurse and acute care nurse practitioner who has cared for critically ill and injured patients since 2009.

positions.stance: Supports a "planned step-by step transition to universal healthcare" and expanding Medicare drug price negotiation to all insurance plans.
Supports targeted tax relief for middle-class families, cracking down on price-gouging, and protecting SNAP benefits.
Will seek federal funding for grid modernization and ensure AI data centers help pay for the grid upgrades they require.
Supports shifting school funding away from property taxes and opposes "unaccountable voucher programs."
Will protect Social Security and Medicare from cuts or privatization and opposes raising the retirement age.

H8TX27049.name: Michael Cloud
H8TX27049.bio: U.S. Representative elected in 2018; member of the House Appropriations and Oversight Committees.

positions.stance: Committed to ensuring the U.S. military has the resources to secure trade routes, deter enemy nations, defend allies, and protect liberty.
Works to protect the right to keep and bear arms; says "the Second Amendment is not about hunting – it is about protecting ourselves from a tyranny."
Supports completing the border wall, designating certain cartels as Foreign Terrorist Organizations, and increasing CBP personnel on the border.
Says the nation must keep its promise to veterans and ensure they have access to quality health care and education.
Wants the region to lead as a major exporter of American energy and has prioritized expanding energy export capability.

H4TX27089.name: Tanya Lloyd
H4TX27089.bio: Public school teacher for nearly two decades who earlier worked in car dealerships, accounting, and real estate.

positions.stance: Running "to spearhead an American Rural Revival" to revitalize rural communities facing hospital closures, drought, and farmland loss.
Supports "a fully government-funded single-payer healthcare system" and restoring access to reproductive health services, including abortion.
Supports breaking up agribusiness monopolies and redirecting farm subsidies to small, diverse, sustainable farms.
Supports equitable funding for rural schools, higher teacher pay, universal early childhood education, and year-round free school meals.
Says agricultural policy "must put conservation and stewardship first" and that agribusiness should pay farmers a fair, living price.

H2TX23082.name: Henry Cuellar
H2TX23082.bio: U.S. Representative for Texas's 28th District since 2005; former Texas State Representative and Texas Secretary of State.

positions.stance: Calls tariffs "hidden taxes" and backs his American Consumer Tariff Rebate Act to put money back in families' pockets.
Supports securing the border and deporting violent criminals, but opposes spending billions to detain children and separate families; favors "smart enforcement" and efficient legal pathways.
Says he will not be "a rubber stamp for either party" and that representatives answer to the people, not their party.
Supports securing the border, stopping illegal crossings, and enforcing the law, alongside practical, bipartisan immigration reform.
Will fight to lower taxes for working families and small businesses, cut federal regulations, and stop wasteful spending.
Believes leadership means representing everyone, not just one party, and pledges to put the people of TX-28 first.
Wants to bring Texas values to Washington: "Less bureaucracy, more action" and "More accountability, less politics."
Supports clear, fair crypto regulations that encourage growth, protect financial freedom and privacy, and keep innovation in the United States.

H8TX29052.name: Sylvia Garcia
H8TX29052.bio: U.S. Representative for Texas's 29th District since 2019 and Vice Ranking Member of the House Financial Services Committee.

positions.stance: Says "protecting democracy means protecting our rights, our freedoms, and our way of life," and opposed redrawing Texas congressional maps.
Fighting to raise wages, expand access to jobs with real benefits, and strengthen career paths; a proud supporter of organized labor.
Working to make housing more affordable, from helping first-time homebuyers to expanding the number of affordable housing units.
Supports the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act.
Fighting to pass the Women's Health Protection Act to safeguard access to abortion and IVF.

H6TX29122.name: Martha Fierro
H6TX29122.bio: Former health care worker at the Texas Medical Center who has mentored small business owners.

positions.stance: Wants to make healthcare more affordable by "raising competition, expanding access, and protecting patient choice — not imposing government mandates."
Supports school choice and parental rights: "Expand educational freedom and strengthen family values."
Wants to cut federal spending and fight inflation to lower costs for gas, groceries and housing, and supports oil and natural gas.
Supports Border Patrol and stopping policies that encourage illegal crossings and human trafficking.

H6TX30245.name: Frederick Haynes III
H6TX30245.bio: Senior Pastor of Friendship-West Baptist Church in Dallas for more than four decades.

positions.stance: Opposes the payday and car title loan industry: "no one should be trapped in cycles of debt simply because they are poor."
Will fight to cap interest rates nationally, close loopholes for predatory lenders, and strengthen consumer protections and fair lending laws.
Supports expanding access to affordable housing, childcare, healthcare and paid family leave, and wage growth tied to the real cost of living.
Will advocate federal investment in under-resourced neighborhoods, support for minority-owned small businesses, and transit, broadband and climate-resilient infrastructure.
Says environmental injustice results from policy choices, including zoning that placed polluting facilities next to Black, Brown and neglected communities.

H6TX30211.name: Everett Jackson
H6TX30211.bio: Small business owner and community organizer.

positions.stance: Will fight to bring high-paying jobs and investment to Congressional District 30 so local businesses can thrive.
Committed to confronting cartels, advocating the death penalty for traffickers, and standing firm against China's aggression.
Will work to protect people of faith from discrimination and foster religious freedom across the nation.
Supports increasing the Child Tax Credit and ensuring public schools focus on "genuine education, not divisive indoctrination."
Dedicated to making DOGE cuts permanent and continually reducing discretionary spending.

H2TX31044.name: John Carter
H2TX31044.bio: U.S. Representative for Texas's 31st District and former District Judge for the 277th District Court in Williamson County.

positions.stance: Supports President Trump's actions to close the border to illegal immigration and deport criminal aliens; has backed reinstating Remain in Mexico.
Believes in "peace through strength" and supports President Trump's effort to rebuild the military.
Says every veteran should receive the care and benefits they've earned; authored the Veterans Transplant Coverage Act.
Supported the Working Families Tax Cut and believes in balanced budgets, limited government, and economic freedom.
"The right of the people to keep and bear arms shall not be infringed"; opposes restrictions on gun ownership and backdoor registries.

H6TX31094.name: Justin Early
H6TX31094.bio: U.S. Army veteran and cybersecurity architect at Dell Technologies.

positions.stance: Will protect Social Security from privatization, remove the income cap on contributions, and expand benefits.
Will push for guaranteed paid family leave and guaranteed vacation time, and protect workers from being fired for being sick.
Will pass legislation to keep human oversight of AI, including ensuring AI never controls machines that could harm people or decides to launch nuclear weapons.
Will fight for responsible data center planning with local input, stricter noise rules, and making data centers pay their fair share for the grid.

H6TX32217.name: Dan Barrios
H6TX32217.bio: Richardson City Council member since 2023 and former public school teacher.

positions.stance: Wants billionaires and corporations to pay their fair share, including raising the corporate tax rate and closing the carried interest loophole.
Won't take dark money and pledges a no-nonsense effort "to clean up corruption and restore accountability—on both sides of the aisle."
Opposes voucher programs that divert funds from public schools; supports better teacher pay, early childhood education, and career pathways.
Supports strengthening the ACA, restoring enhanced premium tax credits, and letting every American, regardless of age, join Medicare.
Supports expanding the Child Tax Credit and paid family leave, and defending the separation of church and state.

H6TX32225.name: Jace Yarbrough
H6TX32225.bio: Air Force veteran and conservative constitutional lawyer.

positions.stance: Will ban insider trading by members of Congress, protect Social Security and Medicare, and work to lower energy and grocery costs.
Supports President Trump's mass deportation efforts and will oppose all amnesty efforts "whether they come from the left or right."
Will champion national concealed carry reciprocity and repeal of the National Firearms Act.
Supports reducing additives and chemicals in food and will stand up for medical freedom against vaccine mandates.
Will hold China accountable for unfair trade practices and promote manufacturing and infrastructure in Texas.

H8TX32098.name: Colin Allred
H8TX32098.bio: Former U.S. Representative for Texas's 33rd District, former NFL linebacker, and civil rights attorney.

positions.stance: Will fight to abolish ICE, moving criminal investigations to the FBI and DEA and border management to CBP with congressional oversight.
Supports the Dream and Promise Act and a pathway to legal status for undocumented immigrants with continuous residency and clean records.
Wants to repeal Trump's tariffs, with targeted national security exceptions, and reassert Congress's authority over trade policy.
Supports the Price Gouging Prevention Act to prohibit price gouging on groceries and consumer goods nationwide.
Wants to reverse cuts to renewable power and eliminate energy tariffs to lower Texans' utility bills.
Wants immigrants vetted and says the U.S. must "not allow an invasion of tens of thousands crossing our border illegally daily."
Supports "Peace through Strength" and says the U.S. should stop selling land to China, especially around military bases.
Says the U.S. can switch to natural gas for all electricity now generated from coal.
Says the correct laws are in place with photo ID requirements for voting.
Favors more focus on mental health and enforcing existing laws, and no-parole prison sentences for gang members.

H6TX15162.name: Vicente Gonzalez
H6TX15162.bio: U.S. Representative and South Texas attorney who founded the Law Offices of V. Gonzalez and Associates in McAllen.

positions.stance: Committed to policies that promote economic stability and protect working families as costs rise.
Supports safeguarding programs that provide seniors financial security and access to healthcare: "These benefits are not privileges."
Supports policies that protect individual freedoms and allow women to make informed decisions about their lives and futures.
Believes every student deserves access to a quality education, "regardless of background or zip code."
Dedicated to ensuring veterans and their families have access to the benefits, healthcare and resources they deserve.

H6TX34080.name: Eric Flores
H6TX34080.bio: Former Texas Army National Guard infantry captain, Assistant U.S. Attorney, city attorney, and municipal judge.

positions.stance: Will bring federal funds to South Texas and hold federal agencies accountable when they slow projects that create good-paying jobs.
Will oppose reckless federal spending that fuels inflation, cut red tape, and support affordable housing solutions.
Will fight for federal funding for roads, bridges and ports, and expanded rural broadband.
Will fight for federal investment in water infrastructure and long-term regional water planning.
Will work to reduce VA wait times, fully fund veterans' benefits, and expand mental health and suicide prevention resources.

H6TX35087.name: Carlos De La Cruz
H6TX35087.bio: Retired 20-year U.S. Air Force veteran and San Antonio small business owner.

positions.stance: Wants to keep securing the border and ensure Border Patrol has the tools, manpower and support it needs.
Will work with President Trump to bring back jobs, lower costs, and rebuild an economy that works for working families.
Says veterans need "Fast care, no red tape, no excuses" from the VA.
Will stand with parents and fight to keep biological men out of girls' sports.
Will press Mexico to deliver the water it owes Texas agriculture and stop foreign competitors from undercutting farmers.

H6TX35095.name: Johnny Garcia
H6TX35095.bio: Bexar County Sheriff's Deputy and SWAT hostage negotiator for nearly two decades.

positions.stance: Says lowering everyday costs is his top priority, including ending the war in Iran and ending "reckless tariffs."
Won't trade stocks in Congress and wants to stop members from profiting on insider information.
Supports Border Patrol resources, an ICE focused on criminals, and comprehensive reform with pathways to citizenship and work visas.
"I don’t believe in defunding the police"; says communities are safest with well-trained law enforcement.
Will crack down on private equity buying up homes and work to lower construction costs to make new homes more affordable.

H6TX02079.name: Brian Babin
H6TX02079.bio: U.S. Representative for Texas's 36th District since 2015, health care provider, and veteran.

positions.stance: Says securing the borders is his top immigration priority; supports the border wall and cutting funding for sanctuary cities.
Will fight to repeal and replace Obamacare with policies that "restore health care freedom in America."
Supports fixing the Windfall Elimination Provision affecting Texas teachers and other measures to help public education.
Supports making the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act tax cuts permanent.
Favors pro-growth policies and fewer burdensome regulations to create jobs in America.

H4TX14111.name: Rhonda Hart
H4TX14111.bio: Disabled veteran who receives her care through the VA.

positions.stance: Opposes Texas's voucher plan "completely" and wants more investment in public schools, teacher pay, and support staff.
Believes in climate change and supports serious investment in renewable energy, especially solar and wind, without quitting fossil fuels overnight.
Criticizes ICE operating masked with no body cameras and "virtually no accountability"; says "No human being is illegal."
"I will not support the SAVE Act. Period."; calls requiring a Real ID to vote a poll tax.
Wants to stop unnecessary Middle East wars, reverse the transgender troop ban, and fully fund veterans' care.

H2TX35144.name: Greg Casar
H2TX35144.bio: U.S. Representative, Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, and former labor organizer and Austin City Council member.

positions.stance: "Working families deserve good jobs, Medicare for All, and affordable education."
Co-sponsors the Freedom to Vote Act and supports ending the filibuster and expanding the Supreme Court.
Co-sponsors the Women's Health Protection Act to protect the right to an abortion nationwide.
Supports the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, abolishing the federal death penalty, and legalizing marijuana with expunged records.
Believes immigrant families deserve to live free from fear of separation, deportation or discrimination, including the right to apply for citizenship.
